title: Pâte à Choux: The All-Purpose Dough for Profiteroles, Gougères, and Gnocchi
summary: This video presents pâte à choux as a universal, versatile dough that can be used for both sweet and savory dishes. The host walks through the classic double-cooking method: starting the paste on the stovetop, then binding it with eggs (emphasizing one-at-a-time addition and a food processor option to vent steam), and finally baking to produce crisp, hollow puffs. The demonstration covers practical technique for piping and shaping, plus several ready-to-plate variations: sweet profiteroles filled with ice cream and topped with chocolate, savory gougères with cayenne and Gruyère, and a gnocchi alla parisienne made from choux dough. Throughout, the video emphasizes steam-leavening (no commercial leaveners) and time/temperature control to achieve lift and crisp shells, with tips on batching, storing, and finishing sauces and fillings. All recipes and techniques are presented as ways to leverage one dough for multiple dishes.
